newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges trade busier after long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges trade busier after long weekend.

text.p: Euro fuel barges traded slightly lower but busier on Tuesday as bunker demand picked up after the long holiday weekend, dealers said.
But cargo markets were again quiet, with most people already looking beyond Thursday's European holiday to next week for a revival in business.
High sulphur barges traded at $81 and $81.50 fob, down $2 from Monday's close, although a number of traders said offers were artificially high late yesterday.

Some participants said there was a lot of product available, pressuring prices, but others said the market was balanced and expected little change in numbers in what they anticipated would be a dull week.
With swaps at $83.00/$83.50 for May one trader saw some upside, but another said paper's strength related more to spread plays with the Singapore market.
Bunker demand was reasonable at up to 20,000 tonnes.
Both high and low sulphur cargo markets were somnolent, although one trader was rumoured to be bidding for a cargo of Scandinavian one percent fuel to cover an African requirement.
"Today it is more than quiet," said one dejected trader.
Physical prices nudged up $1 on a notional basis as swaps firmed slightly.
